title: Qui tollis
readingOutcome: Resolve antecedent, case and function of relative pronouns.

authoringPolicy.method: short concept introduction → authentic example → guided recognition → controlled manipulation → liturgical reading → retrieval
authoringPolicy.vocabularyPolicy: Only the frozen Lesson 17 allocation is introduced; later verbs in relative clauses are explicit support.
authoringPolicy.authenticTextPolicy: Relative-pronoun parsing is anchored in the Ordinary and Vulgate clauses.
authoringPolicy.copyrightPolicy: Pedagogical prose and exercises are original synthesis.

sources.sourceLatin: Agnus Dei, qui tollis peccata mundi: miserere nobis.
sources.provenanceNote: qui has antecedent Agnus and functions as subject of tollis.

sources.sourceLatin: Qui sedes ad dexteram Patris, miserere nobis.
sources.provenanceNote: qui is nominative subject; dexteram introduces the lesson noun dextera in a familiar clause.

sources.sourceLatin: Qui propter nos homines et propter nostram salutem descendit de caelis.
sources.provenanceNote: qui takes its gender/number from the antecedent while its nominative case comes from being subject of descendit.
cuius is genitive singular of qui/quae/quod; the pronoun case comes from its role inside the relative clause.

sources.sourceLatin: Omnis enim quicumque invocaverit nomen Domini, salvus erit.
sources.provenanceNote: quicumque gives the indefinite relative 'whoever' in an authentic soteriological clause.

sources.sourceLatin: Qui cum Patre et Filio simul adoratur et conglorificatur: qui locutus est per Prophetas.
sources.provenanceNote: Two relative clauses allow repeated antecedent/case resolution; later deponent locutus est remains support until Lesson 19.

casePanel.policy: All six cases remain active. Relative-pronoun case is determined by the pronoun's role in its own clause, not by the antecedent's case.

relativePronounFramework.principle: Gender and number come from the antecedent; case comes from the relative pronoun's function inside the relative clause.

pronounSpiral.focus: Relative qui/quae/quod; antecedent versus pronoun case.

learningBlocks.title: A relative pronoun does two jobs

learnerCopy.en: qui/quae/quod points back to an antecedent and also performs a grammatical role inside its own clause. Its gender and number come from the antecedent; its case comes from what it is doing in the relative clause.
learnerCopy.fr: qui/quae/quod renvoie à un antécédent tout en remplissant une fonction grammaticale dans sa propre proposition. Son genre et son nombre viennent de l'antécédent ; son cas dépend de sa fonction dans la relative.

learnerCopy.en: qui refers to Agnus and is nominative because it is the subject of tollis. The antecedent does not force the relative pronoun to copy its case.
learnerCopy.fr: qui renvoie à Agnus et est au nominatif parce qu'il est sujet de tollis. L'antécédent n'impose pas au relatif de copier son cas.

learningBlocks.title: cuius shows the relative pronoun changing case

learnerCopy.en: cuius is genitive: 'whose / of which'. The form is the same across masculine, feminine and neuter singular. This makes it a useful anchor for separating antecedent agreement from clause function.
learnerCopy.fr: cuius est au génitif : « dont / duquel ». La forme est la même aux trois genres du singulier, ce qui aide à distinguer accord avec l'antécédent et fonction dans la proposition.

learnerCopy.en: When you meet a relative pronoun, ask in order: What is the antecedent? What gender/number must the pronoun have? What role does it perform inside its own clause? Only then translate.
learnerCopy.fr: Devant un relatif, demandez successivement : quel est l'antécédent ? quel genre et quel nombre le pronom doit-il avoir ? quelle fonction exerce-t-il dans sa proposition ? Traduisez ensuite.

learnerCopy.en: quicumque means 'whoever'. It behaves like a relative form with an indefinite force. The clause remains structurally readable because nomen Domini and salvus erit are already largely familiar.
learnerCopy.fr: quicumque signifie « quiconque ». Il se comporte comme un relatif à valeur indéfinie. La phrase reste lisible grâce à des éléments déjà largement connus comme nomen Domini et salvus erit.

learningBlocks.title: The pronoun spiral now has three families

learnerCopy.en: By Lesson 17, personal pronouns, is/ea/id and relative qui/quae/quod all live on the same case map. The course will now require you to choose the correct family as well as the correct case.
learnerCopy.fr: À la leçon 17, les pronoms personnels, is/ea/id et le relatif qui/quae/quod vivent tous sur la même carte des cas. Il faut désormais choisir la bonne famille autant que le bon cas.

authenticPassages.sourceLatin: Agnus Dei, qui tollis peccata mundi: miserere nobis.
authenticPassages.instructionalDisplay: Agnus Dei, qui tollis peccata mundi: miserere nobis.

translation.en: Lamb of God, who takest away the sins of the world: have mercy on us.
translation.fr: Agneau de Dieu, qui enlevez les péchés du monde : ayez pitié de nous.

authenticPassages.sourceLatin: Qui sedes ad dexteram Patris, miserere nobis.
authenticPassages.instructionalDisplay: Qui sedes ad dexteram Patris, miserere nobis.

translation.en: Thou who sittest at the right hand of the Father, have mercy on us.
translation.fr: Vous qui êtes assis à la droite du Père, ayez pitié de nous.

authenticPassages.sourceLatin: Qui propter nos homines et propter nostram salutem descendit de caelis.
authenticPassages.instructionalDisplay: Qui propter nos homines et propter nostram salutem descendit de caelis.

translation.en: Who for us men and for our salvation came down from heaven.
translation.fr: Qui, pour nous les hommes et pour notre salut, descendit des cieux.

translation.en: Of whose kingdom there shall be no end.
translation.fr: Et son règne n'aura pas de fin.

authenticPassages.sourceLatin: Omnis enim quicumque invocaverit nomen Domini, salvus erit.
authenticPassages.instructionalDisplay: Omnis enim quicumque invocaverit nomen Domini, salvus erit.

translation.en: For whosoever shall call upon the name of the Lord shall be saved.
translation.fr: Car quiconque invoquera le nom du Seigneur sera sauvé.

authenticPassages.sourceLatin: Qui cum Patre et Filio simul adoratur et conglorificatur: qui locutus est per Prophetas.
authenticPassages.instructionalDisplay: Qui cum Patre et Filio simul adoratur et conglorificatur: qui locutus est per Prophetas.

translation.en: Who together with the Father and the Son is adored and glorified: who spoke through the Prophets.
translation.fr: Qui, avec le Père et le Fils, est conjointement adoré et glorifié ; qui a parlé par les prophètes.

exercises.prompt: What determines the gender and number of a relative pronoun?
exercises.explanation: The antecedent supplies gender and number.

exercises.prompt: What determines the case of a relative pronoun?
options: its function inside the relative clause
the tense of the main verb
exercises.expectedAnswer: its function inside the relative clause
acceptedVariants: its function inside the relative clause
exercises.hint: Case is local to the pronoun's own clause.
exercises.explanation: Relative case comes from its grammatical role inside the relative clause.

exercises.prompt: What case is qui in Agnus Dei, qui tollis...?
exercises.hint: It is the subject of tollis.

exercises.prompt: What case is cuius in Cuius regni non erit finis?

exercises.expectedAnswer: Qui refers to the person being addressed in the Gloria

exercises.hint: The relative clause describes 'Thou who sittest'.
exercises.explanation: The relative identifies the addressee, not the nearby nouns.

objectives: Resolve antecedent separately from relative-pronoun case.
Learn the core singular forms of qui/quae/quod.
Introduce quicumque/quisque/unde without confusing their functions.
Continue the pronoun spiral inside authentic Ordinary/Credo clauses.
